## What it is

- The **Jazz Bass** came out in **1960** as the Deluxe Model; its neck is narrower at the nut than the Precision's (Wikipedia, "Fender Jazz Bass").
- Two **single-coil** pickups, two pole pieces under each string (Wikipedia).
- At first it had stacked knobs (a volume and tone per pickup). From **late 1961**: a volume for each pickup and one tone (Wikipedia). This page models that.
- From 1960 to late 1970 the pickups were **3.6 in** apart; then the bridge pickup moved **0.4 in** nearer the bridge (**4 in** apart). Fender says 1972 (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- There is no switch: the two **volume** knobs blend the pickups. Turn one to 0 and the other plays alone.
- The two pickups are reverse wound and reverse polarity, so "all hum will be canceled when both pickups are at full volume" (Wikipedia). One alone hums.
- Both full up give "the classic scooped, 'growling' sound" (Wikipedia): the two combs add, some harmonics cancel.
- Two coils in parallel have less inductance than one: the blend's resonance is higher, a brighter edge.
- The 70s spacing puts the bridge pickup nearer the bridge: brighter (players say so; Wikipedia). Compare **Jazz 1960s** and **Jazz 1970s** on [Electric Basses Compared](bass-compare.qmd).

## The controls

The Jazz Bass's control area, drawn after the real one (positions approximate). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), then press a ▶ button. The sound is this site's physical model of a plucked bass string through these pickups and this wiring, into an amp; nobody has compared it with a real bass. The picture under the buttons shows the harmonics of the open A string (55 Hz) at the jack (bars) and the circuit alone (line).

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="jbass" data-set="{}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Both full up.</b> The scooped, growling blend. Hum cancels: turn on <b>mains hum</b> and listen.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="jbass" data-set="{&quot;vol2&quot;:0}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Neck alone (bridge volume 0).</b> Rounder, close to a P-Bass. With mains hum on, it hums.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="jbass" data-set="{&quot;vol1&quot;:0}" data-play="lead"><p><b>Bridge alone (neck volume 0).</b> Thin and bright, a nasal bark: a lead bass sound.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="jbass" data-set="{&quot;vol1&quot;:6}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Neck at 6, bridge full.</b> A blend leaning to the bridge pickup.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="jbass" data-set="{&quot;tone&quot;:3}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Both up, tone at 3.</b> Darker, the growl softened.</p></div>
```
